heading: Finite-difference numerical values differ from analytical force/stress
symptoms: Numerical finite-difference force or stress differs from the analytical expression, sometimes only for one or a few values.
suggested_actions: treat this as a possible cutoff discontinuity artifact before changing the model
try changing the VDW cutoff by about 1e-3 Angstrom as a diagnostic
prefer force-shifted VDW potentials when cutoff discontinuity is the cause
do not rewrite force-field parameters unless the discrepancy persists away from the cutoff
text: RASPA manual troubleshooting says finite-difference checks can differ from analytical force/stress when a finite cutoff places a displaced particle outside the cutoff while the original position was inside, especially for shifted or truncated Van der Waals potentials.

heading: Excess loading is negative
symptoms: Computed excess adsorption becomes negative, often in high-pressure isotherm conditions.
suggested_actions: check whether the requested pressure is above the vapor pressure or outside the gas-phase isotherm range
flag the result as a physical-condition issue rather than a runtime crash
ask the user to revise pressure/temperature if the condition is physically invalid
do not patch force-field files to force positive excess loading
text: RASPA manual notes negative excess loading can occur when an isotherm pressure crosses from gas to liquid adsorption or when outside-crystal fluid density grows while loading inside remains near maximum.

heading: Large drift in Monte Carlo energies
patterns: Large drift in Monte Carlo energies
symptoms: Monte Carlo running energies and recomputed final energy disagree; results should not be trusted.
suggested_actions: treat energy drift as a serious failure even if the job reaches DONE
check custom Monte Carlo moves if present
check force-field consistency and missing interactions before accepting output
rerun only after resolving the underlying energy bookkeeping or interaction issue
text: RASPA manual says large Monte Carlo energy drift should not happen and signals an error in one of the Monte Carlo routines; running energies and recomputed energies should match within about 1e-5 or lower.

heading: Energy is not conserved in molecular dynamics
patterns: Energy is not conserved in molecular dynamics
symptoms: Molecular dynamics energy is not conserved.
suggested_actions: reduce the MD time step
add or lengthen equilibration before production MD
check whether the initial system is far from equilibrated
do not accept production results until energy conservation is restored
text: RASPA manual says MD energy non-conservation usually happens because the time step is too large; at initialization, the system can also be far from equilibrated and require a smaller time step.

heading: RASPA hangs at initialization
symptoms: RASPA appears to hang or stall during initialization while trying to create molecules.
suggested_actions: diagnose by setting CreateNumberOfMolecules 0
reduce the initial number of molecules if too many are inserted
for systems without a framework, consider increasing the box size
check packing/loading before changing force-field parameters
text: RASPA manual says if RASPA hangs at initialization, set CreateNumberOfMolecules 0 to check whether too many molecules are being added to the system.

heading: Segmentation fault from incorrect input format
symptoms: RASPA segfaults, possibly because an input definition file has inconsistent counts or malformed sections.
suggested_actions: validate molecule and framework definition file section counts before retrying
check bond, bend, torsion, and following sections for line-count mismatches
regenerate the molecule/framework definition if topology counts are inconsistent
avoid blind simulation.input edits when the crash is caused by malformed definition files
text: RASPA manual says segmentation faults can happen when input is incorrect, for example a file lists 4 bonds but contains 5 lines, causing bends and later sections to be read wrongly.

heading: Mean-square displacement is not linear
symptoms: MSD does not become linear in time, making diffusion analysis unreliable.
suggested_actions: check whether the system is effectively one-dimensional and single-file diffusion applies
increase simulation length before computing diffusivity
verify molecule-molecule and molecule-framework interactions are defined
do not patch output analysis to force linearity
text: RASPA manual lists several causes of non-linear MSD: single-file diffusion, too short simulation time, or missing interactions between molecules.

heading: Minimization does not converge
suggested_actions: if the system wants to change angles but cannot, try minimization using NPT-PR with cell type Regular or RegularUppertriangle
if electrostatics are not accurate enough, increase EwaldPrecision to 1e-10
check whether cell/angle constraints are physically compatible with the structure
do not repeatedly retry the same fixed-cell minimization without changing constraints or precision
text: RASPA manual says minimization may fail when the system wants to change angles but is not allowed, causing non-vanishing stress; it suggests NPT-PR with Regular/RegularUppertriangle cell type or increasing EwaldPrecision to 1e-10.

heading: Molecule cannot be grown
symptoms: CBMC or molecule creation fails because the molecule cannot be grown.
suggested_actions: check molecule definition connectivity and bond definitions
regenerate the molecule .def file if bonds are wrong
verify the requested molecule definition matches the guest model
do not fix this by changing thermodynamic conditions alone
text: RASPA manual says if a molecule cannot be grown, check whether the connectivity and bonds are correct.

heading: Framework flies apart
patterns: intra framework Van der Waals interactions
symptoms: Flexible framework geometry becomes unstable or flies apart.
suggested_actions: check framework bond definitions
check whether electrostatics are computed as intended
check whether intra-framework VDW interactions are enabled or intentionally disabled
route persistent failures to structure/framework definition review rather than only simulation.input patching
text: RASPA manual says if the framework flies apart, check bonds for the framework and whether electrostatics and intra-framework Van der Waals interactions are computed.

heading: Flexible framework energy not conserved near 180 degree bend
patterns: Energy during molecular dynamics with a flexible framework is not well conserved
symptoms: Flexible framework MD energy is not conserved, especially in zeolites with near-linear Si-O-Si bends.
suggested_actions: check for bends approaching 180 degrees that make torsion angles undefined
consider a smoothing function for energy and force contributions as the angle approaches 180 degrees
review Bend/Torsion cross potentials before changing unrelated settings
reduce timestep only as a diagnostic if the underlying torsion singularity remains
text: RASPA manual says zeolite flexible-framework energy conservation can fail when the Si-O-Si bend angle becomes 180 degrees, causing an undefined torsion angle; it suggests smoothing energy/force contributions.

heading: Detected bonds/bends/torsions for flexible framework are wrong
symptoms: RASPA detects the wrong number of intra-framework bonds, bends, torsions, or related potentials.
suggested_actions: check pseudo_atoms.def radii values for framework atom types
remember connectivity is based on the crystal structure even when starting from a restart file
regenerate or correct framework/pseudo atom definitions before retrying dynamics
do not treat this as a mere output warning if topology is wrong
text: RASPA manual says intra-framework connectivity uses a table where atoms are bonded when their distance is smaller than 0.56 + ri + rj, with radii specified in pseudo_atoms.def; wrong radii are the likely cause of wrong detected topology.

heading: Oxygens connected to aluminum not converted to Oa
symptoms: Oxygens connected to aluminum are not automatically converted to the expected Oa type.
suggested_actions: set ModifyOxgensConnectedToAluminium yes when the force-field model expects Oa typing
verify the framework atom typing before changing LJ parameters
check pseudo_atoms.def contains the expected O and Oa definitions
text: RASPA manual says to use ModifyOxgensConnectedToAluminium yes when oxygens connected to aluminum type O are not automatically converted to Oa.

heading: Strange behavior with cations and CBMC reinsertion
symptoms: Numerical instability or strange behavior occurs for cations or net-charged molecules during CBMC reinsertion.
suggested_actions: set ReinsertionProbability to zero as a diagnostic
use RandomTranslationProbability for charged ions when reinsertion causes numerical problems
treat charged-ion CBMC instability as a move-protocol issue rather than a CIF issue
check molecule charges and electrostatics before accepting results
text: RASPA manual says charged molecules in CBMC can have very large or very small Rosenbluth weights; to test this, use RandomTranslationProbability and set ReinsertionProbability to zero.

heading: CIF atoms and pseudo_atoms.def precedence
patterns: definition in the pseudo_atoms.def file has priority
symptoms: Framework atom typing, charges, or pseudo-atom definitions differ depending on CIF and pseudo_atoms.def contents.
suggested_actions: if framework atom definitions from CIF are wrong or incomplete, check pseudo_atoms.def overrides
prefer correcting pseudo_atoms.def for type-level charge/mass/radius issues
check CIF atom names/types match available pseudo atom definitions
do not assume CIF values are used when pseudo_atoms.def defines the same atom type
text: RASPA manual says CIF files can provide framework atom information and those atoms are added to pseudo-atoms, but if also provided in pseudo_atoms.def, the pseudo_atoms.def definition has priority.

heading: ForceField file loading order and working-directory override
symptoms: RASPA reads force-field data from local or installed files, and missing or local override files can change interactions.
suggested_actions: check whether pseudo_atoms.def, force_field_mixing_rules.def, or force_field.def exist in the working directory and override installed force-field files
remember force_field.def overwrites general mixing-rule interactions with specific pair interactions
when patching force-field errors, prefer creating local validated copies instead of modifying installed defaults
verify the ForceField name points to the intended installed directory
text: RASPA manual says ForceField reads pseudo_atoms.def, then force_field_mixing_rules.def, then force_field.def; if any of these files are in the working directory, they are read and used instead of the installed force-field files.

heading: CutOffVDW and force-field tail/shift/truncation behavior
symptoms: VDW cutoff, shifting, truncation, or tail correction choices affect energies and force behavior.
suggested_actions: check CutOffVDW before changing force-field parameters
remember shift/truncation/tail correction behavior is specified in force-field files globally or per interaction
for cutoff-related numerical artifacts, adjust cutoff or force-field cutoff treatment consistently
do not silently change cutoff for production without recording provenance
text: RASPA manual says CutOffVDW controls the Van der Waals cutoff and that shift/truncate/tail-correction behavior is specified in force-field files globally or per interaction.

heading: CutOffChargeCharge and Ewald guidance
symptoms: Electrostatic cutoff or Ewald settings may be inappropriate for the cell size or charge method.
suggested_actions: for Ewald with large unit cells, consider a charge-charge cutoff about half the smallest box length
for non-Ewald methods, use as large a cutoff as practical, greater than about 30 Angstrom according to the manual
check ChargeMethod and EwaldPrecision when electrostatic accuracy is suspected
avoid changing charge cutoffs without checking cell dimensions
text: RASPA manual says CutOffChargeCharge is used with Ewald precision to compute wave vectors and alpha; for Ewald with large cells, about half the smallest box length is advisable, while for non-Ewald methods a large cutoff greater than about 30 Angstrom is recommended.

heading: Grid interpolation accuracy check
symptoms: Tabular grid energies/forces disagree with full computation; output relative errors are too large.
suggested_actions: ensure the grid was generated with the same force field, cutoff, and settings as the current run
increase interpolation density by reducing grid spacing if the structure requires it
regenerate grids when force-field or cutoff settings change
treat large grid interpolation error as invalid output, not a harmless warning
text: RASPA manual says used grids are tested in the output and relative energy error should be smaller than about 0.001; otherwise the wrong grid is used or the structure needs higher interpolation density.
